quad.A.title: High deposits, low dollars
quad.A.text: An outflow reduces credit more (coefficient of banks with a high retail share: -3.09 points of loan growth per standard deviation, against -0.44). As funding shifts to wholesale, pass-through to lending rates would become stronger (from about 70% to 80% after one year, from 100% to 120% after two) and pass-through to deposit rates would rise from about 10% to over 30%.
quad.B.title: Both high
quad.B.text: Exposed to deposit substitution like quadrant A and to already sizeable dollar funding like quadrant C.
quad.C.title: Low deposits, high dollars
quad.C.text: Little exposed to losing deposits, but already funded wholesale and in dollars: for banks of this kind a 25 basis point increase in the policy rate does not reduce lending significantly (+0.29 against -1.33 for banks with little dollar funding), and the reaction to US monetary policy is stronger.
quad.D.title: Both low
quad.D.text: The least exposed on both channels.
note.level.s: The level is a survey-based estimate, not a measurement.
note.level.d: The level comes from an ECB survey in 11 countries that the ECB itself calls experimental, extended to 21 countries with stated assumptions. The two other routes attempted did not confirm it.
note.levelFormula.s: Survey-based estimate, not a measurement: units × share of holders × average amount × dollar share.
note.levelFormula.d: Estimate from a survey in 11 countries that the ECB calls experimental, extended to 21. The two other routes attempted did not confirm it. The formula: units × share of holders × average amount × dollar share.
note.credit.s: Credit figures are orders of magnitude, not forecasts.
note.credit.d: The credit reduction applies coefficients from ECB Working Paper 3199, estimated on individual banks, to national aggregates: orders of magnitude, not forecasts. Cumulative effect over 24 months.
note.flow.s: The outflow rests on assumptions: adoption by country is not observed.
note.flow.d: The outflow assumes that the stablecoins were bought with bank deposits in the chosen share, and that the allocation across countries follows the chosen rule: adoption by country is not observed.
note.band.s: The range combines three uncertainties; it is not a confidence interval.
note.band.d: The range combines three uncertainties: the level (the amount scaled like the estimate's interval, from {a} to {b} around a centre of {c}), the share funded out of deposits (from 50% to 100%) and, for credit, the low and high coefficients. It is not a confidence interval.
note.flag.s: A flag marks an unusual value: it is not a leading signal.
note.flag.d: The flag marks unusual values of the index. The pre-registered test of predictive content for deposits found none: it is not a leading signal of outflows.
note.ranking.s: The ranking orders funding structure, not the probability of outflows.
note.ranking.d: The ranking orders the structure of funding, not the probability that deposits leave. Click a country to open its sheet.
note.country.s: The position describes funding structure: it is not a judgement on banks.
note.country.d: The position orders the structure of funding relative to the other countries: it is neither a probability of outflow nor a judgement on the soundness of banks. These are national aggregates: within a country banks differ.
note.map.scen.s: Scenario indicator: it depends on the assumptions; grey countries are outside the euro area.
note.map.scen.d: The outflow assumes that the stablecoins were bought with bank deposits in the chosen share, and that the allocation across countries follows the chosen rule: adoption by country is not observed. Grey countries are not part of the euro area. Luxembourg, Malta and Cyprus are also shown enlarged below the map. Click a country to open its sheet.
note.map.struct.s: Structural indicator: it does not depend on the scenario; grey countries are outside the euro area.
note.map.struct.d: Structural indicator: it does not depend on the scenario. Grey countries are not part of the euro area. Luxembourg, Malta and Cyprus are also shown enlarged below the map. Click a country to open its sheet.
note.channels.s: The coefficients describe the quadrants; they give no figures by country.
note.channels.d: Coefficients estimated on individual banks, applied here to whole countries: they describe the quadrants, they do not give figures by country. The dashed lines are the medians of the 21 countries. For eight countries the dollar measure comes from the quarterly BSI, which at the median is {r} of the BIS measure: rescaled to the same scale, {list} would change quadrant.
note.monitor.s: The index measures trading against the euro, not holdings or residence.
note.monitor.d: The index measures trading against the euro on centralised exchanges, not holdings or residence. The pre-registered test finds no predictive content for deposits.
note.long.s: The long history is comparable in direction, not in level.
note.long.d: The long history excludes Kraken and Gemini, whose data start later: it is comparable with the main index in direction, not in level.
note.excluded.s: {ex} is excluded from the index over the whole history.
note.excluded.d: {ex} does not respond from the servers that run the automatic update, so it has been removed from the panel for the whole series: local and automatic runs now give the same index. Without it the index is on average {usdt} percentage points for USDT and {usdc} for USDC; the largest gap is {max} points (USDT, week of {w}); flag statuses that change: {n}.
note.missing.s: {ex} did not respond at the last download: recent weeks are computed without it.
note.missing.d: {ex} did not respond at the last download ({n} pairs, {x} of volumes). Its data stop on {d}: later weeks are computed without it, and the EUR share may be slightly lower.
note.share.s: The index is a share: look at the volume before reading a change.
note.share.d: The index is a share: it also moves when the other currencies move. Before interpreting a change, look at the volume against the euro.
note.linktest.s: Pre-registered test: no predictive content for deposits.
note.linktest.d: Pre-registered test of predictive content for households' sight deposits: no predictive content (p = {p}, {n} months). The flag does not anticipate outflows.
note.units.s: The household variant is the consistent one; individuals are an upper extreme.
note.units.d: The survey question refers to "you or a member of your household": the household variant is the consistent one. The individuals variant counts the same household several times and is reported as an upper extreme. The dollar share comes from shares of people, used as shares of value.
note.chartB.s: Percentages measured on the image; the top band is open-ended.
note.chartB.d: The ECB does not publish the data behind the chart: the percentages are measured on the image, with an error of about 0.1 points. The top band is open-ended and accounts for about half of the total.
note.esm.s: The ESM series mirrors world supply and the exchange rate, not the euro area.
note.esm.d: The ESM series mirrors world supply and the exchange rate: the share is constant, so it holds no information on the euro area as such. The shaded band is the interval of the own estimate, which refers to November 2025. The latest ESM value uses the single exchange rate of the programme; the earlier points use each month's rate.
note.criterion.s: Reference level adopted by decision, overriding the original criterion.
note.criterion.d: Reference level by decision of 25 November 2026, taken after seeing the results and overriding the criterion of report 08, which was not met. Outcome of the original criterion: publish only the minimum of the bottom-up estimate.
note.criterionMet.s: The original criterion on the three estimates is met.
note.criterionMet.d: At least two of the three central estimates lie within a factor of 3: the criterion set in report 08 is met.
note.sources.s: If a source does not respond, the last valid data are kept and flagged here.
note.sources.d: If a source does not respond, the corresponding module keeps the last valid data and the status "last valid data" appears here. If a single exchange weighing less than 2% of volumes does not respond, the week is published without it and the source is marked "partly updated"; above 2% the week is held back. The indicator in the side bar summarises this status.
note.fx.s: One exchange rate for the whole programme.
note.fx.d: Every conversion between dollars and euros uses the same rate: the latest ECB reference rate at the date of the supply in circulation. The ESM assumption therefore has one value throughout the application.
note.coef.s: Estimated on individual banks; applied here to national aggregates.
note.coef.d: Estimated on individual banks; applied here to national aggregates and, in the Banks section, bank by bank. Verified against the original, Tables 1 and 3 included.
note.banks.public.s: Public bank-level data, not supervisory data; the order is not a judgement on soundness.
note.banks.public.d: These are public bank-level data from the EBA transparency exercise, not confidential supervisory data, and the order of banks is not a judgement on their soundness. The balance sheets are consolidated at the highest level, so they include activities outside the euro area, and refer to {d}, while the national balance sheets used for the scenario are those of {m}.
note.banks.scenario.s: Each bank loses the same share of deposits as its country: adoption by bank is not observed.
note.banks.scenario.d: The scenario gives each bank the same share of deposits lost as its country, applied to the bank's consolidated deposits: which banks' customers actually buy stablecoins is not observed. The credit reduction uses the high coefficient of ECB Working Paper 3199 for banks above the retail-share threshold and the low one for the others; the credit variant chosen in the simulator does not apply here.
note.banks.usd.s: No dollar exposures in the EBA data: exposures to US counterparties are a different quantity.
note.banks.usd.d: The transparency exercise has no currency breakdown, so dollar funding and dollar assets of individual banks are not available. The column shows original credit exposures to US counterparties as a share of total exposures: it is published only when the United States is among a bank's ten largest countries ({n} banks) and it is not a measure of dollar exposure.
note.banks.coverage.s: Coverage compares different perimeters and can exceed 100%.
note.banks.coverage.d: Coverage is the total assets of the sample banks over the total assets of the country's banks. The first measure uses resident monetary financial institutions (BSI, June 2025, unconsolidated); the second the consolidated assets of all banks in the country (ECB consolidated banking data, second quarter of 2025). Sample banks are consolidated groups with subsidiaries abroad, so the ratio can exceed 100% and is an order of magnitude. No bank of the exercise is based in: {list}.
note.banks.compare.s: Bank by bank, credit per euro of outflow sits between module 5's threshold variant and the uniform rule.
note.banks.compare.d: Module 5 applies one coefficient to a whole country; here the high or low coefficient is applied to each bank and the result is summed by country. The two differ wherever a country below the threshold has banks above it, or the reverse. The bank-by-bank figure covers only the sample banks and depends on the deposit type chosen, not on the amount.

tour.title: Guided tour
tour.1.title: Three results at a glance
tour.1.text: This page states what the programme finds at the latest data: the estimated level, the countries most exposed on each channel and the effect of a high-adoption scenario. Each sentence is filled in from the data.
tour.1.try: Read the three cards, then move on to build a scenario of your own.
tour.2.title: Build a scenario
tour.2.text: The panel on the left sets how many dollar stablecoins are held, how much was paid for out of deposits and how the outflow is allocated. Results update at once, with a range and the caveats under each chart.
tour.2.try: Pick the preset "ESM high 2030" and watch deposits to be replaced and the credit reduction change.
tour.3.title: See it on the map
tour.3.text: The same scenario by country. The country with the highest value is already selected: its panel shows the figures and opens the country sheet. Small countries are enlarged below the map.
tour.3.try: Change what is coloured to "Structure: dollar liabilities" and see a different set of countries stand out.
tour.4.title: Down to the single bank
tour.4.text: The scenario applied to 85 banks from public EBA data. Banks with a high retail share take the high credit coefficient; applied bank by bank, the result lands close to the uniform rule.
tour.4.try: Filter by country, then click a row to open a bank's sheet.
tour.5.title: Watch it week by week
tour.5.text: The weekly share of stablecoin trading against the euro, updated every Monday, with a rule that flags unusual weeks. It measures trading, not holdings, and it does not anticipate deposit outflows.
tour.5.try: Switch to USDC and to the long history; then see "Method and data" for sources and limits.
